title: Citizenship voting deadline, housing costs and pension changes
summary:
A Supreme Court deadline brings fresh urgency for citizens affected by the Ley de Nietos voting suspension. We cover mortgage costs, rental rules, self-employed contributions, pension changes and plans to widen breast cancer screening.

Enjoying Spain Daily? Support us: https://buymeacoffee.com/spanified

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Those overseas election envelopes arriving soon—

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: —don't guarantee a vote for citizens affected by the Ley de Nietos suspension.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: The envelope itself isn't enough? right Hold on.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Exactly. The envelope arrives, but the right to vote still needs a certificate.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Good morning! It's Saturday, the twenty-fourth of October, and this is Spain Daily, from Spanified dot com!

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: I'm Dima, here with Inna. Today: rising mortgage costs, and changes that could restore some suspended pensions.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: First, the court deadline over voting rights for people granted citizenship through the Ley de Nietos, the grandchildren's law.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: The Supreme Court wants the government to name more than a hundred and sixty thousand people affected by the voting suspension. Europa Press reports the deadline is three o'clock on October twenty-eighth. Overseas election mailings begin today. Affected citizens naturalised under the Ley de Nietos need certification proving descent from exiles to vote on November twenty-ninth.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Wait, Dima. Does the certificate have to come from the consular registers, rather than the electoral register?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: From the consular registers. The court has ordered an explicit warning that electoral registration is provisional.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Is proving a Spanish grandparent enough on its own, or do the exile circumstances matter too? good question

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: They do, Inna. The certificate must establish exile under the law's conditions, including the required loss or renunciation of nationality.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: By October twenty-first, only ninety-one certificates had been issued. Very few of those affected are likely to be able to vote.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Ahead of that election, King Felipe the Sixth has called for democratic commitment beyond voting. La Vanguardia reports he spoke yesterday at the Princess of Asturias Awards in Oviedo. He urged daily care for institutions and defended the inclusive spirit of the nineteen seventy-eight Constitution.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Huh. His emphasis was on what citizens do between elections, not just the choice they make on polling day.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: He also told citizens they carry a very high responsibility in defining the country's political direction on November twenty-ninth. mm

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: For homebuyers, borrowing is becoming more expensive. Expansión reports banks are raising mortgage prices and becoming more selective as higher property prices slow sales. The average rate on new mortgages edged above three percent in July. The twelve-month Euribor, the key benchmark rate, is also at its highest since August twenty twenty-four.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Oof. Slower sales, but not an easier mortgage application? That's an awkward combination if you're trying to buy.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And Bankinter was the first to move this month, raising the mortgage prices advertised on its website.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: And bankers expect the slowdown to intensify from now on.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Staying with housing, Consumer Affairs wants two portals to remove thousands of tourist-flat adverts presented as seasonal rentals. El Diario reports most detected listings are in the Madrid region. Rules under the October sixth decree set a thirty-day maximum for tourist rentals and a thirty-one-day minimum for seasonal lets.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Hold on. Calling a tourist flat 'seasonal' on a website doesn't settle which rules the listing has to follow.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's what the ministry is challenging. Madrid neighbourhood associations say many flats use the seasonal label to avoid needing a tourist licence. right

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: There are tax changes for landlords too. El Confidencial reports Cabinet-approved decrees would set personal income tax reductions on net rental income between fifteen and a hundred percent. The scale concerns leases signed from December first. The applicable reduction would depend on the rent, the tenant and the property's area.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Ah, the decision point is signing the lease. Not sitting down with the tax return afterwards.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Precisely. Owners considering a new contract would need to consider those conditions when agreeing the rent and tenancy.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Behind those housing measures is a growing affordability gap. El País reports a Comisiones Obreras union study comparing home prices with wages. Between twenty thirteen and this year, prices rose a hundred and eight percent, while average wages rose thirty percent. Unions want housing included in wage negotiations.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: That's quite a gap. A pay rise can feel very different when the home you're saving for moves further away.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And unions have just backed a general strike with housing as a central theme. true

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Uncertainty also affects self-employed budgets. Cinco Días reports Social Security hasn't approved next year's contribution tables or convened talks with autónomo groups. The election call threatens the review required under the twenty twenty-two agreement. Advisers expect current brackets to continue, but recommend allowing for a possible increase applied retrospectively.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Hang on. Could someone budget using the current payment, then face an increase covering months already gone?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: That's the possibility advisers are allowing for. As an autónomo, I'd rather leave some room than assume the payment stays unchanged.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: One adviser says that if nothing is approved, Social Security would simply extend this year's brackets.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Some pension recipients have a new opportunity to apply. Twenty Minutos reports a decree in force since October twenty-first allows reinstatement of certain suspended pensions. It concerns old rules preventing receipt of both a widow's pension and another contributory pension. Applicants must still meet the remaining requirements and apply by October twenty-first next year.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Oh, that's welcome. Who exactly does it cover?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: People who had a widow's pension under the former rules, for those sixty-five or over married at least fifteen years, and certain unmarried couples. The suspension must come from those old rules.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: A separate pension change took effect yesterday. Twenty Minutos reports some compensation for personal injury is now excluded from income tests for non-contributory pensions. The exclusion covers legally recognised or court-set amounts, but not amounts paid after a ruling or agreement. It may help affected recipients qualify for a pension or keep one.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Ah. So receiving compensation for harm doesn't necessarily mean that money is counted when pension eligibility is assessed?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Within the stated conditions, that's the change. For affected applicants, the compensation's legal basis and payment circumstances matter.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: El País reports PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has pledged to exempt minimum-wage earnings from personal income tax. People earning the current minimum already pay nothing in practice through a deduction. Employers initially withhold tax, which the Tax Agency later refunds.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Wait, so the timing still affects someone's cash: money can leave their payslip before being refunded?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Exactly. Paying nothing overall can still involve waiting for that refund through the tax return.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: On a more serious note, El Diario reports the Audiencia Nacional has applied the amnesty law to twelve Catalan CDR activists accused of terrorism. The court closed their case, finding the acts covered by the law and not serious human rights violations. The decision follows the EU Court of Justice's ruling upholding the law.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Separately, Europa Press reports anti-corruption prosecutors allege former Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero may have committed embezzlement. They say he accepted valuable Saudi jewels without handing them to the state heritage office. Prosecutors are assessing a possible offence; there has been no court ruling on that allegation.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And a potentially helpful health-service change: Twenty Minutos reports a draft order would expand breast cancer screening to women aged forty-five to seventy-four. The National Health System's Interterritorial Council approved the draft yesterday. Regions would introduce the expanded programme gradually after the order enters into force.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Today's practical thread: voting documents, new leases and pension applications all come with conditions that affect what happens next.
